newsitem.title: USA: Chronimed to suspend Quick Check shipment.
newsitem.headline: Chronimed to suspend Quick Check shipment.

text.p: Chronimed Inc said Monday it plans to suspend all shipments of Quick Check Reagent Strip in the United States, citing unresolved issues among itself, its supplier and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Chronimed said its board of directors has approved negotiations to acquire the manufacturing rights of Quick Check from the supplier, Diagnostic Solutions Inc. Buying the rights is the option the company said it prefers at this point.

"We are extremely disappointed to find that the matters that we believed to be settled are not," Maurice Taylor II, chairman, president, and chief executive officer, said in a statement. "There continue to be regulatory problems that just do not get resolved, including the possible need for a new 510(k) clearance."
Earlier this month Chronimed said an agreement had been reached between the supplier and the FDA, and its supplier had been authorized to resume immediate shipment from certain lots.
The FDA had raised questions about the consistency of the strips' test results, and shipment was voluntarily stopped in late December.
The company said it is taking action to gain control of the "entire Quick Check environment."
"In the short term, this will mean a disruption in supply of the product, but it is intended to make for a much more attractive long run opportunity for Chronimed," Taylor said.
Chronimed said it will not yet revise its recent revenue and earnings projections pending the receipt of further information.
The company said Quick Check is not critical to Chronimed's long-term success, but it does represent an attractive profit stream.

Earlier this month, Chronimed projected third quarter revenues of $28 million and earnings of $0.08 to $0.10 a share. It said the adverse effect of reduced Quick Check shipments at that time was estimated at $3 million in revenues and $0.05 a share in earnings.

Chronimed had estimated revenues for the full year ended June at $120 million and earnings of $0.50 a share. On an annualized basis, the Quick Check reagent strip contributes about $12 million in revenue and about $0.15 per share in earnings, the company said.

Chronimed said it is actively pursuing the restructuring of its relationship with Diagnostic Solutions, including owning and controlling Diagnostic, selling its distribution rights to Diagnostic or terminating the relationship.

Chronimed said it prefers to buy the manufacturing rights to the product and move manufacturing to an existing Chronimed facility. It said start-up at a Chronimed facility and the possible need for new clearance would mean shipment disruption of six to 12 months.

The company said the risks associated with controlling Quick Check are acceptable, because Chronimed already has significant internal competency in reagent strip manufacturing. In addition, profit margins would significantly improve, it said.
"We believe the reagent strip meets very acceptable performance standards," Taylor said. "However, to keep it, we must have it on our own terms."
